about: MrSurvivor's change log, read by the admin's Change Log (js/fork/change-log.js, admin menu). One entry per player-facing change, newest day first. k: new | buff | nerf | change | fix | removed (buff/nerf: the thing named got stronger/weaker). s: all (everyone) | lab (Lab runs or the Lab setting) | admin (admin and tools). a: area. t: what changed. n: the numbers, was -> now (optional). c: the commit(s), when known. A commit that changes the game adds its lines here (CLAUDE.local.md); node fork/test-changes.cjs checks it. skip: game-file commits with nothing a player would notice.

days.title: Lab leaderboard, a bar per boss, Choice Band pick, move dex, EV auto-pick in co-op, End run, Keep them apart nerf, less memory in long runs, Skip under the machine, TM descriptions, contract rewards and progress, gems in the coin bubble, the endgame wall, late bosses keep up, a harder Eternatus, temples, dungeons and wormholes, relics, the Necrozma raid at 45:00, English review, trading, the collection shows shinies and radiants, sound only in a focused tab

items.t: The game is silent while its tab is in the background or another window has the focus, and the sound comes back by itself when you return (the music goes on where it stopped).

The Pokémon screen shows each Pokémon as the shiny or radiant you use; only your partner did, and the others showed it only once you clicked them. Changing it in the detail card changes its picture in the grid too.

At 45:00, once Eternatus is beaten, everyone travels to Ultra Space to fight Necrozma. It drinks the light: the screen darkens and at full dark you lose 8% of your max HP a second while it heals. Breaking one of its 4 prisms brings the light back and exposes it for 7 s; otherwise its Prism Armor halves your damage. Photon Geyser and a sweeping Prismatic Laser to dodge, and at half HP Ultra Burst makes it all faster. 3:30, or the run ends.
Beating Necrozma gives a x25 rainbow ticket, 3 gems, half your HP and two relic picks, and the run goes on.
Between the two raids rifts stop opening 2 minutes before 45:00, as they do before 30:00.
The Dynamax Cannon is named as what knocked you out (it said an enemy's area attack).

From 20:00 rare sites rise on the map (a gold arrow points to them, 2:30 to get there): an Ancient Temple, a Mystery Dungeon or an Ultra Wormhole. Walk in and a seal closes around it: the horde is driven off and a strong guardian fights you there; nobody leaves until it falls or the time runs out.
Ancient Temple: a Regi whose stone seal takes 90% off every hit; light the four rune plates by standing on them to shatter it and strike while it is exposed.
Mystery Dungeon: a Monster House of two waves (the second all elites with affixes), then the Dungeon Lord, a pseudo-legendary whose allies each cut the damage it takes by 15%.
Ultra Wormhole: an Ultra Beast that dives between three wormholes and charges out of them; break the Ultra Cores it leaves behind or each one gives it a Beast Boost.

Beating a site's guardian gives coins, tickets, 2 gems, half your HP and a relic pick: your next level-up is a hand of three relics, bonuses that last the whole run and stack (more HP, damage, cooldown, toughness, regeneration, crits, coins and XP, speed, a move level each, or a revive).
No wild legendaries appear while a site's seal is closed, and the Eternatus raid waits for a site fight to end.
While any obelisk stands, a Dynamax barrier (a red dome) cuts the damage Eternatus takes by 80%: the obelisks have to be broken.
items.n: full damage -> 20% while an obelisk stands

items.t: The raid has three stages: at 60% HP three new obelisks rise (their healing stops at 60%) and the Dynamax Cannon fires warned beams at each player; at 25% Eternamax: faster, more beams, and 2 of the 6 crystals shatter.
items.n: Eternabeam every 15 s -> 15 / 12 / 9 s; cannon 20% of your HP a beam, every 7 s then 4.5 s

items.t: Eternatus's HP also follows the team's damage meter, and one hit takes at most 5% of it.
items.n: 45 s of your single-target damage -> the most of that and 40 s of the team's power; no cap -> 5% a hit

items.t: The raid lasts longer to fit its stages.

From 15:00 bosses, wild legendaries and rift legendaries get HP from the team's own damage (a power meter of the best single-target damage per second), so a strong build can't one-shot them: they last at least that many seconds of your damage.
items.n: no floor -> boss 17 s / wild 11.5 s / rift 22 s of your damage at 30:00, 24 / 16 / 30 s at 45:00, 31 / 20.5 / 38 s at 60:00

items.t: From 20:00 one hit takes at most 10% of a boss's max HP.
items.n: no cap -> 10% of max HP per hit

items.t: Past 30:00 bosses grow like the horde: more HP and harder hits (they give more XP for it).
Wild legendaries scale with the clock like other bosses.
items.n: at 45:00: 18 800 HP, 138 damage -> 406 000 HP, 715 damage (before the damage-based floor)

items.t: From 20:00 the horde gets stronger and faster the longer the run goes, and past 30:00 it grows exponentially (Megabonk-style), so an endless run ends even with a strong build. Applies to regular enemies as they spawn.
Past 30:00 a growing share of regular enemies are elites and some carry an elite affix, even below the enemy cap.
items.n: extra elites 0 -> 25% at 45:00, 50% at 60:00; extra affixes 0 -> 15% at 45:00, 30% at 60:00

items.t: Regular enemies' XP from 20:00 grows with the square root of their extra HP, so levels keep coming as the horde toughens.
A THREAT multiplier next to the clock from 20:00 shows how much tougher the horde is (red and pulsing past 30:00).
Radiant Ritual: "Fill with the commonest" is now "Fill with Most Common", and Open Another says "your 10 most common shinies".
Settings say what they do: the pause countdown runs when you unpause, the marker key's choice is Hold or Toggle.
items.n: Countdown after pausing -> Countdown on resume; Press to switch -> Toggle; Bring markers close -> Gather markers; Mobility moves fire by hand -> Fire mobility moves manually

items.t: About 330 of MrSurvivor's own texts reworded: move and card descriptions, settings, the radiant ritual, prestige, the move dex, the death screen and the admin tools ("heals you for 25%", "deal 20% less damage", "1 move" and "1 level left", not "1 moves" and "1 levels").
Lab move upgrades say cooldown and range like the rest of the game, and Endeavor's and Ruination's descriptions say what they really do.
items.n: -20% recharge -> -20% cooldown; +25% reach -> +25% range

items.t: Three Lab branches are named after the real moves they play like, and Sleep Powder evolves into Spore.
items.n: Shadow Vortex -> Ominous Wind, Shadow Shackle -> Spirit Shackle, Toxic Trap -> Toxic Spikes, Spore Storm -> Spore

items.t: The label under the XP bar says what the underdog bonus is.
items.n: Underdog Bonus +N% -> Underdog +N% XP

items.t: The collection's partner button said "Choose de Partner", and the fullscreen button in Settings said "Log out" while in fullscreen.
items.n: Choose de Partner -> Choose as partner; Log out -> Exit

items.t: About 230 of the game's English texts reworded to read naturally and use one word per thing: run (not game), lobby (not room or party), coins (not PokéCoins), cooldown, moves (not attacks); "You fainted…", "A wild Eevee…" (it said "A Eevee"), "Snow", "infatuated", Blade Forme.
Achievement names in Title Case, and a few renamed.
items.n: Terror of bosses -> Bane of Bosses, Loyal partner -> Loyal Teammate, An eye for shine -> An Eye for Shinies, title Brilliant -> Sparkling

items.t: The Kecleon Shop's hidden-ability item is called Ability Patch, its name in the games.
items.n: Hidden Ability Capsule -> Ability Patch

items.t: The About screen read "Fan game free and non-profit", and the site said co-op with up to 4 friends (co-op is 4 players in all).
items.n: up to 4 friends -> up to 3 friends

items.t: Type: Null and the 13 Paradox Pokémon showed their Spanish names; they now have their English ones everywhere, the site's English Pokédex too.
items.n: Bramaluna -> Roaring Moon, Ferropaladín -> Iron Valiant, Colmilargo -> Great Tusk (and 11 more)

items.t: English texts no longer pick up stray capitals from the game's word-by-word translation pass ("Lab Runs", "Co-op", "a Psychic beam", "FIRE SET").
Trade Pokémon with your friends: Trade in the main menu (or the Trade button next to a friend in Friends) sends a request, and your friend gets a popup like a party invite.

The trade window: search and filter your Pokémon (generation, type, normal / shiny / radiant, rarity, hide the ones they have, sort), put up to 20 up, and see each other's offer as it changes. Hovering a Pokémon (holding it on a phone) shows its stats at Lv. 1 and the nature and ability it would get with you.
You can trade a Pokémon's shiny or radiant form (you keep the Pokémon) or, once it has neither, the Pokémon itself; not your partner.
Both players confirm, then a 3 s countdown that either can stop by unconfirming; any change to either offer unconfirms both. A chat to talk while you trade.

Traded Pokémon arrive fresh: no upgrades, TMs, Mints or Capsules come with them, and the new owner gets their own nature and ability. The upgrades and TMs you bought stay on your account (they're back if you get that Pokémon again).

Nothing leaves your collection until both of you confirm: leaving, closing the window or reloading mid-trade loses nothing (a reload puts you back in the trade), and a trade that finished while your tab was closed is in your save the next time you play.
The coin bubble at the top of the main menu also shows your gems.
Contracts also give 1 candy of their Pokémon when you claim them, on top of the contract coins.
items.n: contract coins -> contract coins + 1 candy

items.t: The 15:00 own-type contract needs 3 moves of the Pokémon's type; other moves no longer spoil it, and a type its Lab evolution brings counts too.
items.n: 3+ moves, every one its type -> 3 of its type, others allowed

items.t: Contract progress shows: the bar is the furthest you got with the moves ("Best: 9:12 of 20:00"), and the pause menu says where each contract stands. The Upgrades screen shows your coins and the Pokémon's contract coins side by side (a teal coin), and each button says how much contract coins pay.
Kecleon shop: every TM shows its move's description; when your partner can learn it (or already knows it), that line comes under the description instead of replacing it.
The slot machine's Skip button is under the machine, centred, instead of next to its lever (the gacha and the Radiant Ritual).

Long runs use less memory: the game kept every Pokémon sprite of the whole run loaded (every enemy wave and boss so far), above its own limit. Now only the ones in play or about to come stay; the others load again if they come back.
items.n: late run: 337 -> ~240 sprite sheets, ~85 -> ~68 Mpx of images (about 70 MB less)

items.t: Keep them apart (turning a bond down) gives less damage, and only the first 5 times in a run; after that it still keeps your moves apart, with no bonus. The button says how many are left.
items.n: +10% per bond, no limit -> +2.5% per bond, 5 at most (x1.13 in all)

items.t: End run: from 20:00 the pause menu has an End run button that ends the run at once with the usual summary and rewards. In co-op it starts a vote: the run ends for everyone only if every player says yes (30 s to answer; one No and it goes on).

Auto-pick EV cards works in co-op too: your cards don't open, the EV card is taken and a small banner says who you're waiting for. Ticking the box with a hand open now takes that hand's EV card at once (it used to leave the menu open).

Move dex: the Pokémon screen has a Pokémon / Moves switch. Moves lists every move (Lab-only ones with the LAB chip), searchable and filtered by type and category; each one shows how it works, its numbers at Lv.1 and max level, its upgrades, its evolution and who learns it.
Choice Band: picking it up (with two or more moves) stops the game and asks which move to lock into; before, it locked whichever move was active when you touched it.

Boss health bars: every boss near you gets its own bar under the clock, nearest first (up to 4, then "+N MORE"); bosses far away don't show, and one off screen has a dimmer bar. Before, only one boss had a bar, wherever it was.
items.n: 1 bar -> up to 4, within ~1.4 screen widths

items.t: Lab leaderboard: Lab runs now go on their own copy of every leaderboard (solo and group; today, week, month, all-time and all-time per Pokémon). The LAB switch next to Solo / Group shows it. Lab runs still never count for the regular leaderboard.

days.title: Lab builds and mechanics, Player Manager, fairer rifts, reward nerfs

items.t: Change Log in the admin menu: every change to the game by day, with what was buffed, nerfed, added or fixed.
Fly and Bounce no longer pin you in place while airborne: you keep walking, and a step taken in the air isn't snapped back.
Close-range moves take a bigger damage cut.
items.n: 25% -> 35% (melee, spin, dash, recoil, every close kind)

items.t: Leaps: untouchable time capped at 60% of the recharge; the 0.6 s after landing only when you land by the target (Dig, Dive). Fly, Bounce, Phantom Force and rolls no longer get the 0.5 s mover grace.
Rollout and Ice Ball swing at the target like melee instead of the way you walk.
Recoil moves cost less HP.
items.n: at most 8% -> 3% of max HP a second

items.t: Bounce, Phantom Force and Parting Shot hit harder.
items.n: Bounce 28 -> 33, Phantom Force 32 -> 33, Parting Shot 10 -> 21 (its mark 30% -> 20%)

items.t: Extreme Speed, Spectral Thief and Sunsteel Strike hit softer.
items.n: Extreme Speed 22 -> 19, Spectral Thief 32 -> 27, Sunsteel Strike 44 -> 39

items.t: Fusion Flare and Vacuum Wave toned down after the balance pass.
items.n: Fusion Flare damage 40 -> 22 (the Fusion combo still doubles it); Vacuum Wave point-blank bonus up to x2 -> x1.6

items.t: Future Sight and Tailwind evolve with their kinds' usual numbers (x1.8 damage; Future Sight also a longer beam and -15% recharge). Taunt now evolves into Embargo. Attract shows pink fairy rings instead of hearts.

Rift legendary wins are the same for everyone: a player who's down when it falls gets up right then (30% HP), and every player gets their own held-item roll instead of one item for whoever stood nearest.
Co-op support moves, only on co-op Lab run cards: Heal Pulse, Aromatherapy, Wide Guard, Block and Helping Hand (evolving into Purify, Teatime, Mat Block, Shelter, Coaching).
Roost's Lab evolution is now Swallow and Reflect's is Barrier.
The 3 s count-in only plays after a stop longer than 10 s (pause, level-up card, item, bond, co-op hold); quick stops go straight back to playing.

27 moves that only differed in numbers get a field each (Rapid Spin speed, Rolling Kick stun, Outrage revenge, Night Slash and Bug Buzz weaken, Razor Leaf crits, Magnitude rolls, Solar Beam heals...). The five spins and four shoves all play differently now.

The 11 melee moves get one trait each (reach, heavy knock, leech, flinch or parry) and none swings 360 degrees any more. Flame Charge stacks speed, leaps land by type, Counter, Mirror Coat and Metal Burst block the hits they store.
Pivot moves: U-turn plus new Volt Switch, Flip Turn and Parting Shot hit and switch you to your next slot.
Dashes, recoil charges and rolls go the way you walk (or at your target when standing still), hit everything on that line and leave you where you started. They only fire when an enemy is on the line.
Evolved names now do what they promise: Avalanche x2 after you're hit, Endeavor brings enemies down to your HP share, Tailwind gives +30% speed to you and nearby teammates.
The admin menu and Player Manager show item and Pokémon names in English (they said Cinta Elección, Código Cero...).
Fusion Flare and Fusion Bolt deal x2 with a bigger blast when cast within 2 s of each other. New Pledge moves: two different Pledges make a fire sea, a swamp or a healing rainbow.
New Lab moves Taunt (snipers charge you instead) and Attract (nearby enemies slowed and can't hit you by contact).
Held items' new icons are the old icons' size again (Choice Band was drawn twice as big).
Enemies near the start of the map were hit twice by area moves (and pushed twice as hard); now once.
With Lab on, Kecleon sells a 9th daily TM: a Lab move the species learns by TM in the games (works in Lab runs only).
Decoys: new Follow Me and Rage Powder leave a beacon that pulls enemies off you; Substitute's doll is a decoy too. Bosses ignore them.
Synergies and recipes hit each neighbour once (some were hit twice).
Bond recipes: some pairs in one bonded slot change a move (Solar Flare, Thunderstorm, Infernal Hex, Deep Freeze, Root Network). The bond screen marks them.
Your run's ability is shown in every run: a tag at the top and a line in the pause menu.
Trade-off boosters: Belly Drum fills every stack for half your HP; new Shell Smash (big boosts, take 35% more) and Curse (costs HP, drains a boss).
Status converters: Venoshock uses up poison for up to x3; new Smelling Salts and Wake-Up Slap deal x3 to stunned or sleeping enemies.
Per-Pokémon contracts: goals for one Pokémon that pay coins for its upgrades (1000-1500 each).
The second starting move has its own Lab pick (a Lab-only pick was silently dropped in normal runs).
Settings > Accessibility > Mobility moves fire by hand (off by default): dashes and charges only go off while you hold fire.
Late-hand cards: Speed and Cooldown keep coming past their cap (up to 4 more, each costs 4% max HP). In the endless after Eternatus every hand has a +1 EV card, with an auto-pick option.
Synergy cards once you own two matching moves: Frost Fire, Overload, Steam Burst, Wildfire, Toxic Drain, Shatter, Quicksand, Nightmare.
Veto goes to 5 levels.
items.n: 3 -> 5 (levels 4 and 5 cost 2,060 and 3,910 coins)

items.t: TM cards come less often until a Pokémon has 2 moves (40% chance to enter the hand).
Prestige now also needs Veto at 5 (it needs every upgrade maxed).
Set bonuses: 3 moves of one type (Fire, Water, Electric, Grass, Fighting), 3 physical moves or 2 priority moves turn on a bonus while you hold them.
Elite affixes near the spawn cap: Shielded, Swift, Vampiric, Splitting, Explosive, named over the enemy.
TMs taught at Kecleon's now work in Lab runs (they did nothing).
Lasting hazards: Spikes and Toxic Spikes stay 60 s, String Shot leaves webs, Stealth Rock leaves pointed stones.
Spin and dash moves take the 25% close-range cut too (recoil always did).

Mobility moves are safer: 0.5 s untouchable after a dash, recoil, roll or leap landing; leaps 0.6 s after landing; recoil cost capped and half refunded on a knock-out; ramp stacks fade slowly instead of resetting.
items.n: leap landing 0.15 s -> 0.6 s; recoil 12% a cast -> at most 8% a second

items.t: A Lab evolution keeps the run's nature and ability slot, and swaps the ability cleanly (old abilities used to stay on).
Branching upgrades: 12 well-known moves offer two Branch cards at level 3 to 4 that change how the move works (Flamethrower into Fire Spin, Heat Wave or Fire Blast...).
XP per kill keeps pace with the run.
Marks: Psychic, Future Sight and Doom Desire stamp enemies; the next hit from another move sets the stored damage off on everything nearby.
Close-range moves aim at what they can reach (they waited for a boss out of reach), and dashes no longer fire at rocks and chests.
Bosses after 15:00: at 18, 21, 24 and 27 minutes, and every 3 minutes from 33:00 in the endless.
A resumed Lab run no longer spawns every boss since 3:00 in its first seconds.
Lab runs have one ability, never two (both used to run).
items.n: Blaze x2.025 -> x1.5, Thick Fat x0.3 -> x0.5 taken

items.t: Lab move lists no longer change with the Pokémon's nature (the picker and the run could disagree).
Legendary upgrade cards give x2 instead of x3 (same as Epic), and count 2 toward the card's cap.
Open Another next to Continue: roll the same gacha pull again, or sacrifice the next 10 shinies in the Radiant Ritual.
Rift legendaries get harder as the run goes on (they fell far behind the regular bosses).
Hover an effect chip in a run to see what it does (stat boost totals, weather multipliers, altar powers, time left).
A LAB switch and an info icon on the Play button.
The Underdog XP ladder shows in a Lab co-op lobby.
Shinies and radiants roll stat boosts every run: N random stats +10% (shiny) or +20% (radiant), N by rarity (Common 4 ... Legendary 1).
The Lab-only +10% / +20% XP and coins for shinies and radiants (replaced by the stat rolls; Lab rerolls stay).
Synthesis heals a share of max HP instead of a flat amount.
items.n: +0.2 HP/s a level (1 HP/s maxed) -> +0.25% max HP/s a level (1.25%/s maxed)

items.t: The team summary's last column says Damage taken (it said Taken).
Life Orb never takes you below 30% HP.
items.n: down to 1 HP -> stops at 30%

items.t: A bond can be turned down: Keep them apart gives every move +10% damage for the run. Bond cards keep their move's description.
Candies a Pokémon's line has left to spend show next to its name.
3 s without damage after any revive (traps and explosions used to knock you straight back down).
The Upgrades screen fits at 4K again after upstream's new row; the Lab evolution bar no longer jumps.
The end screen's tickets line lists rainbow x25 tickets the run gave.
The lobby's Ready Up countdown no longer gets stuck at 0.
Rift legendaries give a rainbow ticket less often.
The Radiant Ritual shows a banner of 3 random silhouettes and odds by rarity (Common 40, Uncommon 30, Rare 18, Epic 9, Legendary 3%).
items.n: Arcanine 54% -> 75%, Mewtwo and Eternatus 23% -> 12.5% each

items.t: The personality test: a new player picks a starter from a grid right away.
Your HP bar sits above your Pokémon instead of the top-left corner.
Missions count in Lab runs (they didn't move at all with Lab on).
The mouse wheel switches move slots in a run.
Gholdengo sometimes carries a rainbow x25 ticket instead of its x10 one.
items.n: 1 in 20

items.t: The ticket count at the top shows rainbow x25 tickets.
Type and physical/special arrows on level-up cards are bigger.
items.n: 9 px -> 12 px

items.t: The weak-side note says how much less: 'does -25% damage' instead of 'hits for only 75%'.
Enemy healers no longer heal themselves (a lone healer topped itself up every cast).
Signature move cards get their type and category arrows.
Starting move: a separate pick for Lab runs, and the picker lists Lab moves (Lab runs silently fell back to the default).
Bewear's Hearts show to teammates.
A Lab run that ended can't be resumed after a reload, and End run just ends it (no summary, no end-of-run coins).
Player Manager: every player's save and live status, give or take coins, tickets, gems and Pokémon, resets, bulk actions, and Join a player's lobby or run.
The Revive card is Legendary rarity and much rarer.
items.n: 1 hand in 25 -> 1 in 100

items.t: The French, Italian, Portuguese and Chinese dictionaries said PokéSurvivor again; MrSurvivor is back.
The Asset Admin publishes from a PC where git has no name and email (the artist's first publish failed).
New held-item icons from the artist: Amulet Coin, Assault Vest, Choice Band, Choice Scarf, Focus Sash, Leftovers, Life Orb, Lucky Egg, Quick Claw, Rocky Helmet, Shell Bell.
New radiants: Wooper, Quagsire, Clodsire.
New radiants: Chewtle, Drednaw.
New radiants: Shaymin, Hydrapple.
New radiants: Arcanine, Eternatus.
Merged PokéSurvivor's big update: Kecleon Shop, natures, abilities, TMs, second starting move and upstream's co-op spectating (it replaces ours; we keep the cut to the first teammate standing).

days.title: Card and gacha rarities, rainbow tickets, prestige, Lab raids and gems, English first

items.t: Settings > Graphics > GUI scale slider; Icon size on one line.
Settings > Accessibility > Auto-shoot (on by default): off, attacks only fire while you hold the button.
The run's end screen fits the screen (it scrolled on long runs).
The last Spanish texts in English: shinies caught, coin breakdown, save dots, move levels, buff chips, personality traits.
Settings fits big screens (at 4K it ran off the screen) and closes on a click outside.
Level-up cards can't be picked for the first second, so a stray click doesn't take one.
English first: the game starts in English unless the player picks another language, and the site and link preview are English. 'Leaf Tornado' no longer shows as 'Leaf Gust'.
The Eternatus raid replaces Arceus's Judgment at 30:00: break 3 obelisks, hide from the Eternabeam, 3 minutes. Win a rainbow x25 ticket each and the run goes on.
Wild legendaries roam the map from minute 15 (one every 75 s, 2 at most).
From minute 15, rift legendaries can come Mega or Primal: x1.3 HP, x1.2 damage and rewards.
Mega Evolution in every run again: from minute 5, each rift legendary you beat may drop your Pokémon's Mega Stone.
items.n: Lab only -> every run, 1 in 30 per rift win

items.t: A solo Lab run survives a reload: Resume or End run from the menu.
Gems, a rare drop (bosses 1, legendaries 2, 0.7% of enemies): 100 gems reset a Pokémon's upgrades with every coin back.
With Lab on, prestiging costs 100 gems.
Defense becomes toughness: +100% = half damage, up to +200%.
Speed stops at x2.5 (the speed card stops coming up there).
Rare Revive card: holds one self-revive (50% HP, 3 s untouchable, enemies thrown back).
Network stats in co-op (each teammate's ping and jitter, your FPS).
Crosshair colour and size, and aiming with the right stick without Manual aim.
A stats panel under your HP bar in runs (damage, speed, HP, defense, cooldown, regen, crits, cards taken).
Opacity sliders for your move effects (100%) and your teammates' (60%).
Half of the Legendaries you pull are ones you don't own yet (while the banner has any).
Upgrade all: max every upgrade of a Pokémon at once, after confirming the cost.
A secret Bewear far south of the start: hug it to unlock Hearts (your shots become hearts).
Prestige (up to 3) once every upgrade is bought: upgrades reset, +5% HP, damage, speed and defense per level; at 3, every run starts with a random held item.
Spend Lab candies on a stat (HP, Attack, Sp. Atk, Defense, Speed), up to 10 points per line, with a refunding Reset.
Rainbow x25 ticket: 25 gacha pulls with a guaranteed Legendary. From rift legendaries (1 in 10), surviving 30:00 and 4 big achievements.
Upgrade cards have rarities: Common, Uncommon x1.25, Rare x1.5, Epic x2, Legendary x3.
A pity bar under the pity line (gold from the soft pity at 180).
The small type arrows over enemies are in every run, not only Lab.
When you're knocked out, a popup says what did it, and the game-over screen shows it with your last hits.
Rain Dance, Sunny Day, Sandstorm and Snowscape make a few seconds of weather around you every 14 s instead of changing the arena's weather.
Mist Ball slows more and longer; slowed enemies show an ice-blue ring.
items.n: 30% for 1.2 s -> 40% for 2 s

items.t: 'Your type' for either of your types; the weak-side note names the category.
Metal Burst stores every hit, Scary Face's upgrades slow more, Protect, Rest and Shell Trap get upgrades that work.
Lab move texts fixed against what the moves really do (sleep, confusion, recoil, Counter, Rest, Shadow Force...).
Moves show what they do (Grass Knot's leaves, Rock Tomb's falling rocks); evolutions no longer named after healing moves; tooltips mention knockback, dash invulnerability and melee's 25% cut.
Going down cuts to a teammate instead of gliding across the map, and the rift trip no longer stutters a downed player's camera.
The pause menu's Continue button works in co-op (only Esc/P did).
A Pokémon, shiny or radiant changed in the menu reaches the room at once; rejoining after a reload works again; lobby cards show radiants.
Soft pity: from pull 180 without a Legendary its chance rises 2 points a pull (pity stays 220). The odds screen shows the next pull's chance.
Lab phase 9: close-range and sustain moves.
Radiant glow slider (Settings > Graphics).
The interface scales to the screen (bigger at 1080p, 1440p and 4K).
Good/bad arrows on level-up cards, the move tooltip and enemy type arrows.
The arrows-with-symbols badge style and its setting (just the 4 plain arrows now).
The artist's arrow icons for the level-up badges.
Asset Admin: a local page to download, replace and publish every sprite and icon, with the Radiants importer and the Sprite Kit.
Merged PokéSurvivor's co-op connection retries, with their relay server switched off (co-op stays direct-only).

days.title: MrSurvivor launches: co-op upgrades, Mega Evolution, Lab mode, radiants

items.t: Guest progress is kept in the browser across reloads and updates, and moves to the account on sign-up or login.
The Radiant Ritual's roll uses the gacha's slot machine, then the radiant's card.
Radiant filter on the Pokémon screen; a radiant you own is played over its shiny by default.
Radiants give more than shinies in Lab runs.
items.n: +20% XP and coins and +2 rerolls (shinies +10%, +1)

items.t: Progress to the next Lab evolution under the HP bar.
Epic and Legendary Pokémon get no Underdog XP.
Shadow Force chains through up to three enemies instead of being a stronger Phantom Force.
23 evolved moves no longer reuse real moves' names; Fly's evolution is Dual Wingbeat.
First radiant: Mewtwo.
The ritual is weighted by each radiant's rarity, and a published radiant works without a game update.
Radiant Admin: import, preview and publish the artists' radiants from a local page.
The Underdog bonus's share of the XP bar is gold, and a ladder shows the bonus by rarity before a Lab run.
Shiny and radiant move colours come from the most vivid changed colour.
Radiant forms and the Radiant Ritual: sacrifice 10 shinies for one radiant at random (asks before a shiny legendary goes).
Radiant Sprite Kit page: download a Pokémon's sheets for the artist, with its rarity.
Random Pokémon in the co-op lobby (your saved partner doesn't change).
Co-op keeps going when the host's tab is hidden (guests were stuck waiting).
The arrow to a Meowth/Gholdengo thief says how far it is.
A Pokémon you own the shiny of plays as shiny unless you chose Normal for it (remembered per Pokémon).
Legendaries are much rarer, with a longer pity.
Screens remember their last tab and the Pokémon screen its filters across reloads.
Lab mode moves to its own Experimental tab in Settings.
Lab mode (Settings > Experimental): real learnsets, 70 abilities, 45 new moves in 10 new kinds, 70 signature moves, evolving during the run, Eviolite, Underdog XP, candies, shiny move colours.
Mega Evolution only drops and works in Lab runs (it came back to every run on 2026-10-21).
Markers to off-screen things sit around your Pokémon (hold or toggle F / Y to gather them); co-op says who is down.
A setting turns off the countdown after the pause.
The level-up box no longer stretches with long descriptions; the bond countdown waits until every screen is clear.
Mega Evolution: winning a rift with a Pokémon that has a Mega gives its Mega Stone; holding it, it Mega Evolves.
items.n: +25% damage, +10% speed, +15% HP, +8% defense

items.t: Stat moves evolve at max level (Swords Dance into Belly Drum...) and then cast on their own from any slot.
Hex's x1.7 also applies to stunned (paralyzed, frozen) enemies, and works for co-op guests.
'+1 projectile' did nothing on 12 moves (Shadow Sneak, Seed Bomb...), and the spread upgrade jumped to a 150-degree fan.
Dragon Dance no longer cuts Swords Dance's time, power or stacks; buff timers no longer round up.
A charge ring over your Pokémon for slow moves (Hyper Beam, Solar Beam...).
Move tooltips say what the move hits with and what boosts it; wrong English move descriptions fixed.
A small 'Critical' label over critical hit numbers.
The very rare card is now Second Nature: stat-boosting moves cast from any slot (about 1 hand in 150, once per run, only with such a move).
Item Mastery, the very rare card from earlier that day (every held item's boost at once); replaced by Second Nature.
Item Mastery, a very rare card (about 1 hand in 150): every stat item's boost without holding them.
Whole-run trolls (freeze, disco, lights out, earthquake, invasion, Thanos snap, piñata), screen flips, teleports, Rare card next.
The admin menu (owner only, ` key): trolls, god mode, level up, heal, drops, coins, tickets and Pokémon; runs where the admin helps themselves don't go on the leaderboard.
Parties survive a reload or an update: your slot waits as Reconnecting; the host drops an absent guest after 90 s.
Random Pokémon: start a solo run with one of your Pokémon, with a minimum rarity.
The buff ring at your feet drains with the time left and pulses near the end.
Clearer notes on level-up cards about a Pokémon's weak and strong side.
Leaving the pause runs a 3 s Resuming countdown with the world frozen.
The gacha's Skip sits next to the slot machine's lever.
The Upgrades screen always opens on your current partner.
Ready Up in the lobby: when everyone's ready a 3 s countdown starts the run.
When you're down in co-op, the camera follows a teammate (Q/E, A/D, LB/RB to switch).
Every player's bond screen opens together instead of one after another.
End of run: team summary (kills, downs, revives, damage dealt and taken) and each move's damage, share, kills and DPS.
Buff timers on their move slot, and an icon size setting.
'Good for you' on stat boosts that match the Pokémon's stronger side.
A Skip button straight to the results.
Quieter defaults and a limiter (some sounds clipped).
Enemies show an arrow with your active move's type multiplier (x4, x2, 1/2, 1/4, x0); cards for a new move of your type say 'Your type'.
Hover a move slot or the held item for its details; drag a slot onto another to swap them.
Hold left click on the map to aim at the cursor.
Power sort (base stat total).
Import a save from the original PokéSurvivor with a transfer code (Settings > Account).
Merged PokéSurvivor's fewer cloud writes (the save uploads on Save); ours also backs up unsaved changes after 10 minutes and when the tab is hidden.
Merged PokéSurvivor's co-op hardening and fixes (guest vortex pull, guest Hex, level-up cards reopening, +1 projectile).
Cloud saves and the leaderboard on MrSurvivor's own server.
The game becomes MrSurvivor: its own name, colours and domain (a fork of PokéSurvivor).
